metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 24-channel Smarting mobi (mBrainTrain) wireless amplifier at 250 Hz using a 10-20 montage. Each trial comprised a 3 s fixation reset, a 1 s directional arrow cue, a 3 s black-screen motor imagery execution period, and a 3 s reset. Classes were rest, left hand, right hand and feet, with each participant performing a subject-specific subset of three tasks over multiple sessions.

citation_details.title: NERVE Attacks: Breaking AI-Powered Brain-Computer Interfaces
citation_details.author: Zahra Tarkhani, Georgios Akkogiounoglou, Lorena Qendro, Isabel Tscherniak, Anil Madhavapeddy
citation_details.abstract: The rapid integration of AI into human-centred systems such as Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) has created a poorly understood attack surface linking neural signals to physical systems. Exploits in this domain threaten cognitive autonomy, mental privacy, and physical safety, from neural data exfiltration to malicious control of BCI-tethered devices. We introduce the NERVE Attacks class, a systematic characterisation of five orthogonal attack dimensions that together span the complete BCI stack: Neuro-mimetic Forgery (N), Evasion via Desynchronization (E), Replay-based Hijacking (R), Vein Tapping (V), and Embedded Backdoors (E). To evaluate this class, we present EEGle, an AI-assisted extensible framework for systematic BCI security analysis. Our evaluation uncovers 17 novel neuro-specific attack instances and reveals a stealth-effectiveness spectrum unique to BCI backdoor design.
